title: Hedgehogs Chew Poisonous Toads and Spit the Venom Over Their Own Spines

scenes.text: A hedgehog licks a poisonous toad. Then it starts foaming.
It chews the toad's skin, works up a thick froth of spit, and twists around to smear it over its own spines.
Some get so lost in the frothing that they fall over.
In 1977, a scientist had volunteers prick themselves with the quills. The toad-coated ones hurt more.
A hedgehog carries up to 7,000 spines. Coat them in toad venom, and a predator's bite wound gets a lot worse.
They'll also froth over leather, old paint and dog poo. Scientists still argue about why. Step one is the same: find a toad.

description:
Hedgehogs practise self-anointing: they chew irritating or toxic material, including the skin of toads, then lick the frothy saliva onto their spines.
A 1977 paper in Nature reported that spines from hedgehogs that had anointed with toad skin were more painful and irritating to volunteers than clean spines; a hedgehog can carry as many as 7,000 spines, and some anoint so intently that they topple over. They also anoint with leather, paint and faeces, so the full reason is still debated.
What is the strangest thing you have seen an animal do?
subject: hedgehog
first_comment: One wild hedgehog's stomach was found holding 283 legs from giant crickets called weta. What is the weirdest animal habit you know?
